question: Evaluate $$\sec^{-1}\left(\sec\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)+\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}\left(\operatorname{cosec}\frac{7\pi}{6}\right).$$
explanation:
Principal value of the inverse secant term
The principal range of $\sec^{-1}x$ is $[0,\pi]-\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$. Since $$\sec\frac{5\pi}{3}=2,$$ the angle in the principal range whose secant is $2$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. Therefore, $$\sec^{-1}\left(\sec\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}.$$

Principal value of the inverse cosecant term
The principal range of $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}x$ is $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]-\{0\}$. Also, $$\operatorname{cosec}\frac{7\pi}{6}=-2.$$ The required principal angle is therefore $-\frac{\pi}{6}$.

Addition of principal values
Hence, the required value is $$\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{6}.$$
